summary: Replica of a rural Japanese fire tower at Japanese Village Plaza, Los Angeles. The 1983 build year rests on one timeline, and the plaza dates conflict.

facts.design: Replica of a fire tower from rural Japan (Yagura Tower)

access.note: The plaza is an outdoor mall that visitors come to. No source says whether the tower itself can be climbed.

events.note: The Impact Fund timeline places the tower under 1983. CBS News and Goldsea date the plaza to 1978 and 1984, so the tower year rests on one source.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: CBS News gives 1978 for the plaza. Goldsea gives 1984 for David Hyun's development of it. The Impact Fund timeline has the plaza starting a year after the 1983 tower. The story reports the dates without choosing one.
Wikidata classes the structure as a fire lookout tower. The Impact Fund describes a replica of a rural Japanese fire tower anchoring the plaza entrance. The story follows the replica description.

notes_for_editor: The 1983 build year is from one source, the Impact Fund timeline, and the plaza dates conflict (CBS 1978, Goldsea 1984). The status was 'standing' but is now 'unknown': the only support is a photo caption in a blog post dated November 15, 2021, and no current source was found. Unfetched leads: a 2010 BlogDowntown article (https://blogdowntown.com/2010/08/5585-japanese-village-plaza-reopens-as-community) and the Wikipedia article 'Yagura (tower)'. A search summary said the original wooden tower was later replaced with a steel one after termite damage. That is not verified and is left out of the story; fetch and check before using it. A Historic Places LA report (hpla.lacity.org/report/3c28aa62-65ef-477a-8200-9f4c63b2b2a0) was listed in search with a 1978 plaza date, but fetch_text found no matching lines, so it is unverified. The brief's coordinates match the Wikidata coordinates. Wikidata's 'fire lookout tower' class does not fit a decorative replica; the record may need a note. No staffing or fire history appears in any source, so none is given.
